options.text: Positive natural-number solutions exist for the square case, but not when $n>2$.
Both equations are Baudhāyana triples under one shared name.
Solutions for $n>2$ are what produce the square-power triples.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Baudhāyana triples solve the square-power equation. Fermat's claim for $n>2$ says no positive natural-number solutions exist for that higher-power equation.

teacher.key_rationale: The square-power equation has Baudhāyana triples; the higher-power equation does not have positive natural-number solutions. Merging both under one name or reversing which equation produces triples misses the hinge.
